area: Big Ambitions modding surface (Build 3672 re-verification): ModEntry attributes/lifecycle, ModContext, enums.txt, AssetService, Harmony feasibility, ModCompatibilityValidator
findings:
All paths below are under the 3672 decompile root C:/Users/maart/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Source-HekWereldBlazor/5bdc82ab-5f56-48c4-88a8-225c84a9ea0b/scratchpad/decomp/ . Net result: the modding surface is essentially UNCHANGED from the 3670 findings, plus one new additive API family (ModdingAPI.RegisterModBusinessType / RegisterModVehicleType) that does NOT extend to skills/roles. === 1. [ModEntry*] ATTRIBUTES, SCOPES, TIMING ===
Attributes live in assembly BAModAPI (BigAmbitions.ModAPI.dll), file BigAmbitions.ModAPI/BigAmbitions.ModAPI.decompiled.cs:535-564. Exactly five, all [AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Class, Inherited=false)], all empty marker types:
  - BAModAPI.ModEntryOnInitializationLoadAttribute  -> ModActivationScope.Initialization
  - BAModAPI.ModEntryMainMenuAttribute              -> ModActivationScope.MainMenu
  - BAModAPI.ModEntryOnCityLoadAttribute            -> ModActivationScope.City
  - BAModAPI.ModEntryOnBlueprintCreatorLoadAttribute-> ModActivationScope.BlueprintCreator
  - BAModAPI.ModEntryOnIntroLoadAttribute           -> ModActivationScope.Intro
Scope<->attribute mapping: BigAmbitions.ModsInternal.ModDiscoveryRegistry.ScopeAttributeMappings, ModsInternal/BigAmbitions.ModsInternal/ModDiscoveryRegistry.cs:17-24. A class may carry several; ModDiscoveryRegistry.DiscoverFromInfosAsync loops all mappings and calls RegisterEntry once per matching attribute (ModDiscoveryRegistry.cs:567-579). Assembly attribute [assembly: BAModAPI.RegisterModClass(typeof(X))] (RegisterModClassAttribute, AllowMultiple=true, decompiled.cs:555-564) is mandatory; GetRegisteredModTypes (ModDiscoveryRegistry.cs:614-658) requires X to be a concrete class in the mod assembly implementing BAModAPI.IModBigAmbitions or it is warned + skipped.

BAModAPI.ModActivationScope enum (ModsInternal/BAModAPI/ModActivationScope.cs): None, Initialization, MainMenu, City, Intro, BlueprintCreator.

Lifecycle driver 1 - HGModLoader (BigAmbitions/BigAmbitions/HGModLoader.cs), a scene MonoBehaviour. Awake/OnEnable -> once Steam is initialised -> InitializeMods() (HGModLoader.cs:58-79): ModLifecycleLoader.Initialize() -> ModDiscoveryRegistry.DiscoverAllModsAsync() -> CheckConflicts() -> ModLifecycleLoader.LoadScopeAsync(Initialization) -> LoadScopeAsync(MainMenu) -> LogFailedMods(). This is at boot / main-menu scene, BEFORE any save is deserialized, BEFORE GameManager exists, and BEFORE AddressableLoader.RegisterAndLoadAll() (the game runs that in SaveGameManager.TryPrepareLoad, SaveGameManager.cs:338-340, and again at :466).

Initialization scope is PERSISTENT: ModLifecycleLoader.LoadScopeAsync treats scope==Initialization as isPersistentScope (ModsInternal/BigAmbitions.ModsInternal/ModLifecycleLoader.cs:99), never unloaded on scene changes, only on Application.quitting (ModLifecycleLoader.cs:64-77). Its OnLoadAsync runs exactly once per process.

MainMenu / City / Intro / BlueprintCreator are TRANSIENT and mutually exclusive: ModLifecycleLoader keeps one CurrentScope; a scene load swaps it. Driver 2 - UI.Load.LoadingScreen.LoadAsyncScenes (BigAmbitions/UI.Load/LoadingScreen.cs:90-123): fade -> ModLifecycleLoader.UnloadScopeAsync(unloadModScope) -> _sceneLoader.LoadScenes(...) -> WaitForAsyncCallsToFinish() -> ModLifecycleLoader.LoadScopeAsync(loadModScope) -> GlobalEvents.InvokeOnGameLoaded(). Scene->scope wiring in UI.Load/LoadScene.cs: LoadGame loads City (LoadScene.cs:41-44), LoadMainMenu loads MainMenu, LoadIntro loads Intro, LoadBlueprintCreator loads BlueprintCreator.

CITY-SCOPE OnLoadAsync timing (critical for the two-role design): it runs AFTER the city scenes finish loading and BEFORE GlobalEvents.InvokeOnGameLoaded(). GameManager lives in a city scene, so GameManager.Awake() (BigAmbitions/GameManager.cs:254) and the EmployeeHelper.Init() it calls (GameManager.cs:299) have ALREADY executed. SkillData is loaded even earlier - AddressableLoader.RegisterAndLoadAll() -> Register<SkillData>("Skills", SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded) (BigAmbitions/BigAmbitions.SaveSystem/AddressableLoader.cs:170) runs synchronously (ForceLoad/WaitForCompletion) inside SaveGameManager.TryPrepareLoad, before the scene loads. So at City OnLoadAsync: game skills loaded, employees initialised, SaveGameManager.Current populated, gameplay not started yet. AddressableLoader.RegisterAndLoadAll re-runs on EVERY save load (SaveGameManager.cs:339 and :466) and there is NO mod-merge step in AddressableLoader.RegisterAll (AddressableLoader.cs:154-179) - so a mod-injected SkillData must be re-injected in City OnLoadAsync on every load, which the timing permits.

BAModAPI.ModEvents.onModsLoaded / onModsUnloaded (public static Action, decompiled.cs:635-640) fire after every LoadScopeAsync/UnloadScopeAsync via InvokeSafely (exception-isolated). Mid-session Steam mod add/remove: BigAmbitions/BigAmbitions/ModsView.cs:191-194 -> ModLifecycleLoader.ApplyScopeChangesAsync.

=== 2. ModContext MEMBERS / SAVE HOOK / LOCALES ===
BAModAPI.ModContext (decompiled.cs:565-579) is a sealed class with exactly THREE members: string ModRootPath, string ModId, IModLogger Logger. Nothing else - no save callback, no game-state accessor, no service locator.
CONFIRMED: there is NO save-data hook in the mod API. Persistence is unchanged: hook GlobalEvents.onSaveGame (public static Action, BigAmbitions/GlobalEvents.cs:28; invoked with a plain ?.Invoke() synchronously before serialization in SaveGameManager.Save, SaveGameManager.cs:174) and read/write SaveGameManager.Current.modData (Dictionary<string,string>) yourself. The save .meta records hasEverUsedMods and activeModsAtLastSave (list of {modId, modDisplayName} from ModLifecycleLoader.GetActiveMods(), SaveGameManager.cs:223-241) - game bookkeeping only, not a mod entry point. GlobalEvents also exposes onNewDay, onNewHour (GlobalEvents.cs:16,18) - both plain Action, plain ?.Invoke(), so a mod handler that throws will abort that tick (the existing StoreManager mod already wraps every handler in try/catch - keep doing that).
BAModAPI.IModBigAmbitions (decompiled.cs:580-587): string[] RelativeAssetBundlePaths {get;}, Task OnLoadAsync(ModContext), Task OnUnloadAsync(). Optional base BAModAPI.ModBigAmbitionsBase supplies RelativeAssetBundlePaths => Array.Empty<string>().
LOCALES: auto-discovered. ModDiscoveryRegistry.SyncDiscoveredLocalizationPaths (ModDiscoveryRegistry.cs:318-344) scans each discovered mod folder for a "Locales" subdirectory and hands {modId -> <modFolder>/Locales} to Localizor.LocalizorManager.SyncExternalLocalizationPaths. ModLifecycleLoader calls LocalizorManager.LoadLocalizationTables(reloadIndex:false) after every scope load/unload (ModLifecycleLoader.cs:88,127,160). Dropping Locales/en.json + Locales/nl.json in the mod root is the supported route (the existing mod already ships exactly this).

=== 3. ModEnumDefinitions / enums.txt ===
BigAmbitions.ModsInternal.ModEnumDefinitions (ModsInternal/BigAmbitions.ModsInternal/ModEnumDefinitions.cs). Reads <modFolder>/enums.txt (const "enums.txt", :11), one line per entry "Namespace.EnumType.ValueName" - last '.' splits type from value (GetModEnums, :132-183). Resolves the Type via Type.GetType(typeName + ", BigAmbitions, Version=0.0.0.0,...") (:159-171), computes BAModAPI.ModEnumHash.GetSafeHash(valueName) (SHA-256 -> Int32, bumped out of the reserved 0..2000 band; decompiled.cs:663-683), and stores (enumType,hash)->valueName plus which mod keys claimed it.
WHAT IT DOES: conflict detection between mods and NOTHING ELSE. The only consumers in the entire 3672 tree are ModEnumDefinitions.GetAllConflictingModsList() -> HGModLoader.CheckConflicts() (HGModLoader.cs:100-110, shows a notification) and ModEnumDefinitions.GetModConflictsList(modInfo) -> BigAmbitions/BigAmbitions/SubscribedModUI.cs:73. A hash collision makes TryDefineModEnums return false, which SKIPS that mod entirely (ModDiscoveryRegistry.cs:453-456).
Grepped the whole dump: ModEnumHash / GetSafeHash / DefinedEnumValueNames appear ONLY inside ModEnumDefinitions. No code feeds these values into the CLR. Enum.Parse, Enum.ToString, and the hand-written source-gen EnumHelpers.ToStringFast switch expressions (BigAmbitions/EnumHelpers.cs - each ends "_ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException", e.g. :52) stay completely unaware of anything in enums.txt.
CONFIRMED for Build 3672 (same as 3670): enums.txt CANNOT add a usable value to an existing game enum. It is purely a "declare that I hash value X into enum T so a collision with another mod is reportable" registry. Any custom skill/role identity must be a plain string, not an enum member.

=== 4. AssetService FULL API ===
BAModAPI.Services.AssetService (decompiled.cs:687-1248), all static. PUBLIC surface:
  - RegisterBundle(string modId, string bundleKey, string absolutePath) : void  (:713) - records a path, does not load. CALLED FOR YOU by ModLifecycleLoader.LoadModInstanceAsync (ModLifecycleLoader.cs:433-447) for each string in IModBigAmbitions.RelativeAssetBundlePaths: bundleKey = path.Replace('\\','/'), absolutePath = ResolveBundleAbsolutePath(modRoot, path). ResolveBundleAbsolutePath (ModLifecycleLoader.cs:469-499) inserts a platform folder: for "Bundles/sm" it tries <modRoot>/Bundles/Windows/sm first, then falls back to <modRoot>/Bundles/sm.
  - GetBundle(string modId, string bundleKey, bool autoLoadIfRegistered = true) : AssetBundle  (:786) - loads on demand from the registered path, caches by "modId/bundleKey". THIS IS THE KEY ENTRY: it returns the raw UnityEngine.AssetBundle, so you call bundle.LoadAsset<Sprite>("name") / LoadAllAssets<T>() directly.
  - GetAllAssetNames(modId, bundleKey) : string[]  (:905)
  - HasAssetCached(modId, bundleKey, assetName) : bool  (:919)
  - IsBundleLoaded(modId, bundleKey) : bool  (:773)
  - FindAssetInAnyBundleByFileName<T>(string fileName) where T : UnityEngine.Object : T  (:1051) - scans ALL registered bundles, matches by path-suffix / filename / filename-without-extension, returns first hit. This is what the base game uses for mod prefabs (BigAmbitions/Helpers/PrefabHelper.cs:46,49; BigAmbitions/ShelfController.cs:256).
  - Spawn(modId, bundleKey, prefabName, Vector3, Quaternion, Transform parent=null, bool worldPositionStays=true, bool active=true, bool remapShaders=true) : GameObject  (:1111)
  - SpawnAsync(... CancellationToken ct) : Task<GameObject>  (:1140)
  - RemapShaders(GameObject root, string fallbackShaderName=null) : void  (:1178) - rebinds materials to in-build shaders by name (bundled shaders get stripped); PrefabHelper/VehicleHelper call it on modded content.
  - UnloadBundle(bundleKey, bool) (:754), UnloadAllBundles(bool) (:733) - loader calls UnloadAllBundles(true) on quit.
NOT PUBLIC: LoadAsset<T> (:935), LoadAssetAsync<T> (:984), LoadPrefab (:1038) are all private.
ROUTE FOR A REAL SKILL ICON Sprite (if runtime Sprite.Create won't do): AssetService.GetBundle(context.ModId, "Bundles/xxx") then bundle.LoadAsset<Sprite>("icon_name"), OR AssetService.FindAssetInAnyBundleByFileName<Sprite>("icon_name"). Note runtime path also works: new Texture2D(2,2).LoadImage(pngBytes) + Sprite.Create(...) - this is exactly how BigAmbitions.ModsInternal.ModThumbnailLoader.CreateSpriteFromPngBytes builds mod thumbnails (ModsInternal/.../ModThumbnailLoader.cs:139-150). So a PNG in the mod folder + runtime Sprite.Create needs no AssetBundle at all; a bundle is only required for a pre-imported Sprite/atlas/prefab/font.
AssetService static state resets only on RuntimeInitializeLoadType.SubsystemRegistration (domain reload), ResetStaticData :1239-1247 - not per scene. Bundles from RelativeAssetBundlePaths are re-registered each time the owning scope loads.

=== 5. HARMONY ===
The game ships NO Harmony. Grepped the ENTIRE 3672 dump (BigAmbitions/, BigAmbitions.ModAPI, ModsInternal, ExternalPlugins, BigAmbitions.AI, BigAmbitions.Characters, Legacy) for Harmony / HarmonyLib / 0Harmony / HarmonyPatch / PatchAll -> ZERO hits. No Mono.Cecil, no MonoMod. BigAmbitions.ModsInternal.csproj references no 0Harmony.dll.
CAN a mod bundle 0Harmony.dll in Dependencies/ and PatchAll in OnLoadAsync? YES, the loader is built for it:
  - BigAmbitions.ModsInternal.ModAssemblyLoader.TryLoadDependenciesAsync (ModsInternal/.../ModAssemblyLoader.cs:135-168) loads every *.dll under <modFolder>/Dependencies/ (SearchOption.AllDirectories, sorted ordinal) via Assembly.LoadFrom, BEFORE the mod's own assembly is loaded/validated (called from ModDiscoveryRegistry.DiscoverFromInfosAsync:519).
  - AppDomain.CurrentDomain.AssemblyResolve is hooked to ModAssemblyLoader.OnAssemblyResolve (ModDiscoveryRegistry.cs:144, :69), which resolves a mod's references from its own folder / its Dependencies/ / other known mod folders (ModAssemblyLoader.cs:100-133) - so the mod DLL binding to 0Harmony resolves.
  - The mod ROOT folder must contain EXACTLY ONE .dll: ModDiscoveryRegistry.TryGetRootDllPath (:687-709) - 0 or >1 -> "Mod not discovered". Harmony MUST go in Dependencies/, never the root.
  - new Harmony(id).PatchAll() in OnLoadAsync is fine (game assemblies all loaded by then, esp. for City scope). For non-Initialization scopes the mod is unloaded/reloaded on every scene change, so patches must be torn down in OnUnloadAsync (keep the Harmony instance, call UnpatchAll(id)) or be fully idempotent.
Another local mod already doing this: not visible in the game dump (local/workshop mod DLLs are user files). The Dependencies/ mechanism + single-root-DLL rule are unambiguously designed for exactly this pattern; community meta-mods commonly ship Harmony this way. The existing StoreManager mod does NOT currently bundle Harmony (RelativeAssetBundlePaths => Array.Empty, no Dependencies/, StoreManagerMod.cs).
LOAD-ORDER CONCERN with two Harmony-bundling mods: ModAssemblyLoader caches loaded assemblies by SIMPLE NAME in a shared dictionary LoadedAssembliesBySimpleName (ModAssemblyLoader.cs:16, :170-201). LoadAssemblyFromPathAsync (:77-98) returns an already-loaded assembly by simple name. So whichever mod is discovered first loads its 0Harmony.dll and ALL later mods share that exact instance/version; their own 0Harmony.dll copies are ignored. Discovery order = Steam mods by steamItemId ascending, then local mods by full path ordinal (ModDiscoveryRegistry.DiscoverAllModsAsync:186-198). Implication: if two mods ship different Harmony majors, the later one runs against the earlier one's Harmony. Harmony 2.x is broadly back-compatible so this usually works, but: ship a current Harmony 2.3.x, use a unique Harmony id string, do not assume your bundled copy is the one in memory. ModCompatibilityValidator does NOT reconcile this (see 6). There is no "duplicate dependency assembly" rejection - the duplicate-assembly check only covers each mod's single root DLL.

=== 6. ModCompatibilityValidator + would our mod pass ===
BigAmbitions.ModsInternal.ModCompatibilityValidator (ModsInternal/BigAmbitions.ModsInternal/ModCompatibilityValidator.cs). TWO checks, BOTH assembly-reference major-version checks only - NO IL / API / content / behaviour inspection:
  1. TryValidateGameAssemblyCompatibility (:13-48): for each AssemblyName the mod DLL references whose simple name matches a LOADED assembly named "BAModAPI*" or "BigAmbitions*" (GameAssemblyNamePrefixes, :11; IsGameAssemblyName :150-161) and that lives outside any mod folder, if referenced.Version.Major != loadedGame.Version.Major -> mod rejected. Minor/patch ignored. Anything not starting with those two prefixes (e.g. 0Harmony, HarmonyLib, ExternalPlugins, DOTween) is NOT checked.
  2. TryValidateModAssemblyCompatibility (:50-95): inter-mod dependency resolution + mod-vs-mod major-version match. Only relevant if our mod depends on another mod's assembly.
CRITICAL: EVERY game assembly is [assembly: AssemblyVersion("0.0.0.0")] - verified for BigAmbitions.dll (BigAmbitions/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:5), BigAmbitions.ModAPI.dll (decompiled.cs:18), BigAmbitions.AI.dll, BigAmbitions.Characters.dll, ExternalPlugins.dll, BigAmbitions.Legacy.dll, BigAmbitions.ModsInternal.dll (ModsInternal/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:5). All major 0. So check #1 is effectively a NO-OP: mod references them at 0.0.0.0, game has them at 0.0.0.0, 0==0, always passes - EVEN when the mod references the full game assembly BigAmbitions.dll directly (which is how you get Buildings.Office.Headquarters.* / Entities.EmployeeInstance / Helpers.EmployeeHelper / BizManBusiness types; the existing mod's asmdef precompiledReferences already lists BigAmbitions.dll). The real game build (3672) is tracked via GameVersion.GetCurrent().buildNumber, not assembly versions, and there is NO runtime build-number gate on mod loading (targetBuildNumber is only checked at UPLOAD time: BigAmbitions/BigAmbitions/UploadModPanel.cs:422, rejecting targetBuildNumber > current build - no runtime effect).
Other discovery-time gates (ModDiscoveryRegistry.DiscoverFromInfosAsync, :430-611): exactly one root .dll; readable assembly metadata + non-empty assembly name; no two mods share a root-assembly simple name ("Duplicate mod assembly name detected", :497-512); enums.txt conflict -> skip; >=1 valid [assembly:RegisterModClass] pointing at a concrete IModBigAmbitions class.
A separate ModValidator with content rules DOES NOT EXIST in 3672 (searched - only ModCompatibilityValidator and the upload-only SteamModUploader).
WOULD a mod that bundles Harmony + patches the HQ BizMan UI + injects a custom SkillData PASS? YES - nothing in discovery or validation inspects what the mod does. Requirements: (a) exactly one DLL in the mod root, Harmony + any other deps under Dependencies/; (b) unique root-assembly simple name; (c) no enums.txt hash collisions with another active mod; (d) valid RegisterModClass attribute. The major-version check is satisfied automatically (all game assemblies are 0.0.0.0). Runtime stability (SkillHelper.GetData NPEs on an unknown skill name, the BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs/SetTab patch surviving City scope reloads, MissingMethodException if 3673 changes a bound signature) is entirely the mod's responsibility - the loader will load a mod that then crashes.

=== 7. NEW IN 3672 vs 3670: BAModAPI.ModdingAPI (main assembly) ===
File BigAmbitions/BAModAPI/ModdingAPI.cs - static class in the MAIN game assembly (not BigAmbitions.ModAPI.dll). Additive registration helpers:
  - ModdingAPI.RegisterModBusinessType(Buildings.BusinessType) / UnregisterModBusinessType(BusinessType|string) -> Helpers.BusinessTypeHelper.RegisterModBusinessType (BigAmbitions/Helpers/BusinessTypeHelper.cs:52-74) + Buildings.BuildingTypeHelper.RegisterModBusinessTypeAvailability (BigAmbitions/Buildings/BuildingTypeHelper.cs:32-47). Registers a new businessTypeName bound to a suitableBuildingType; refuses to shadow a base-game type; ModBusinessTypes dict merged into BusinessTypes on load (BusinessTypeHelper.cs:26-33).
  - ModdingAPI.RegisterModVehicleType(Vehicles.VehicleTypes.VehicleType) / UnregisterModVehicleType(string) -> Vehicles.VehicleTypes.VehicleTypeHelper.RegisterModVehicleType (BigAmbitions/Vehicles.VehicleTypes/VehicleTypeHelper.cs:47-78).
There is NO RegisterModSkill, NO RegisterModEmployeeRole/JobTitle, NO RegisterModManagerPlan, NO HQ-tab registration API anywhere. SkillData still loads via the hardcoded AddressableLoader.Register<SkillData>("Skills", SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded) with no mod merge, re-run every save load. So: the two-native-role design (Filiaalmanager + Team Leader, each with its own custom skill + own HQ BizMan tab) still requires bundled Harmony + reflection - inject two SkillData entries after each OnSkillDataLoaded, Harmony-patch BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs/SetTab (+ Awake) to add tabs, Harmony-guard SkillHelper.GetData against the two new skill names. Native BusinessType/VehicleType registration is a clean seam but does not help roles/skills.
